channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump Kicks Off Asia Visit After US Imposes New Chip Curbs
item.description: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, kicking off his first overseas trip since his party’s decisive defeat in congressional elections.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Sheinbaum Offers ‘New Era’ of Mexico-China Ties After Trade Spat
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum reached out to Chinese leader Xi Jinping during a meeting in Shenzhen on Tuesday, seeking to overcome a recent spat over trade tariffs while steering clear of aggravating US ties.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Soto and Alex Vasquez

item.title: Dutch Coalition Announces New Deal to Avoid Government Collapse
item.description: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said the three parties in the ruling coalition struck a deal to continue working together and avoid an imminent government collapse.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Van Oosterom

item.title: US to Curb China's Nvidia Access as Trump Goes to Asia
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Global stocks extended a recent slump as US moves to restrict China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers added to risk aversion ahead of Nvidia's high-stakes earnings.
President Donald Trump supported calls from some Silicon Valley leaders for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s chief executive officer, despite the chipmaker’s board moving forward with its search for a new leader.
And Anthropic’s planned IPO could generate billions of dollars in demand from index-tracking funds, though the AI startup may have to wait longer than SpaceX did to join two major stock benchmarks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Threatens to Strike Civilian Sites If US Does the Same
item.description: Iran threatened to retaliate against civilian infrastructure located near US or Israeli military bases if those countries targeted similar sites in the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Sykes

item.title: NATO Turns to Commercial Rockets for Greater Space Access
item.description: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is contracting commercial rockets and spaceports to grow its satellite-launch network and help neutralize risks to the space systems on which it relies.
item.dc:creator: Selcan Hacaoglu

item.title: Putin’s War on Ukraine Is Ravaging a Generation of Russian Men
item.description: Vladimir Putin’s war against Ukraine is hollowing out a generation of Russian men and undermining the president’s own efforts to halt the country’s demographic decline.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Kao, Priyanjana Bengani, Alberto Nardelli, Anand Katakam and Daryna Krasnolutska

item.title: Canada's Carney Meets China's Xi in Shenzhen
item.description: China and Canada agreed to further tariff relief on agriculture and steel exports as President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Mark Carney met in Shenzhen on Tuesday. Bloomberg's Minmin Low reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham Says New UK-EU Relationship 'Will Take Time'
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said any major change in the UK’s relationship with the Europe Union would “take time” and wouldn’t be implemented until after the next election in Britain. “We will initiate a discussion with our EU partners about options for our long-term relationship,” Burnham told City of London leaders at a banquet on Monday. Rosa Prince has the details. Her views are her own. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy Says US, Europe Delegates to Hold Peace Talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he held online talks with US and European delegations who made additional plans toward the goal of leader-level peace negotiations. Earlier Monday, President Donald Trump told reporters that a planned trilateral meeting on Thursday in Shenzhen with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping would include a discussion on the war. Bloomberg's Greg Sullivan has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Latvia Taps Bank Economist for Finance Minister in New Cabinet
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs nominated the chief economist of the country’s third-largest bank as finance minister, with the most prominent jobs in his next government going to people with no prior experience in politics.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis

item.title: Trump to Attend ‘Quad’ Economic Security Talks Before Xi Meeting
item.description: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of India, Australia, and Japan on Tuesday for a top-level gathering of their informal security group, an opportunity to reassure key Indo-Pacific partners ahead of Trump’s highly anticipated meetings with Xi Jinping later this week in China.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Philip J. Heijmans and Sakura Murakami

item.title: Trump Set for China Summit With Xi and Putin
item.description: US President Donald Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China for an unprecedented three-way summit following Republican losses in the US midterms. Ahead of the trip, Trump has said he does not expect to raise the case of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang with Xi, while a senior administration official says Ukraine is unlikely to be on the trilateral agenda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Faces More Strikes and Protests Over Cost of Living
item.description: French unions and student groups are planning another day of strikes and protests on Tuesday, testing the momentum of a movement that has brought repeated disruption in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: William Horobin

item.title: Turkey Seizes Last Major Pro-Opposition TV in Police Raid
item.description: Turkish authorities seized control of Sozcu TV, one of the country’s last major pro-opposition broadcasters, in an early-morning police raid, marking the second takeover of a government-critical television channel in just over a month.
item.dc:creator: Ugur Yilmaz and Inci Ozbek

item.title: Mongolia’s President Abruptly Resigns After Claims of Corruption
item.description: Mongolian President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa unexpectedly announced he’ll resign from office while facing allegations of corruption from the opposition in parliament.
item.dc:creator: Terrence Edwards

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin Has World Worried About Great Power Stitch-Up
item.description: At Yalta in 1945, the leaders of three dominant military powers gathered to craft a plan that would bring stability to the world – or conspired to carve it up among themselves.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: New UK Relationship With Europe to ‘Take Time,’ Burnham Says
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said any major change in the UK’s relationship with the Europe Union would “take time” and wouldn’t be implemented until after the next general election.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: UK Milburn Report Calls for Youth Tax Cuts, Tougher Welfare
item.description: The UK should cut taxes for businesses hiring young people while toughening the welfare system in order to tackle youth unemployment, a government-commissioned review into the crisis will say.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain and Irina Anghel

item.title: Trump Backs Huang Comeback While Nvidia Board Seeks New CEO
item.description: President Donald Trump supported calls from some Silicon Valley leaders for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer, despite the chipmaker’s board moving forward with its search for a new leader.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Kate Sullivan
